messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate observed in eu-west1 gateway for inference requests over the last 3m — average 5xx rate 7.4% (baseline 0.3%). Autos failover policy triggered: beginning graceful drain of edgepool eu-west1-a. Paging eu-west oncall.

emma (oncall): on it. seeing the alert. grabbing context, starting timeline.

raj (sre): I can join. are we seeing gateway 502s or backend worker OOMs?

sofia (eng-runtime): from quick metric look: gateway 502 and 504 spikes, plus a correlated increase in mlworker restarts in eu-west1-a. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~15% at the same time.

leo (network): no regional network blips in telemetry. egress and LB healthchecks look fine.

emma (oncall): ok assign action items: raj / sofia debug workers, leo watch routing, i'll coordinate failover options and CS comms. ana, can you prep a short note for customers?

ana (customer-success): (typo) ana: yes on it — will draft status message for impacted customers in EU and hold until we confirm scope.

raj (sre): running quick ps on mlworkers in eu-west1-a: `ssh jmp-eu-west1-a` then `docker ps --filter name=mlworker` — seeing a few workers stuck in RESTARTING. grabbing logs.

sofia (eng-runtime): logs show repeated allocations failing with error `CUDA OOM` in mlworker pod 0-3. Also one worker shows `Unhandled Promise rejection: KV store timeout`.

emma (oncall): CUDA OOM suggests memory pressure. Did any deploys or model swaps happen in last 30m?

sofia (eng-runtime): no deploys. However, traffic pattern shows a long-tail of very long sequences from an internal customer causing increased kv-cache growth and pinned sessions.

raj (sre): dump of pod logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z mlworker-2 ERROR allocate failed: attempted 15872MB > available 12288MB
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z mlworker-2 INFO evicting prefix cache entry 0x7f9b...
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z mlworker-2 WARN KV timeout 2000ms for key session/abc123
```

emma (oncall): OK. Options: 1) increase mlworker pool in eu-west1-a (if capacity available), 2) failover traffic to eu-central while we drain, 3) purge some long-lived cache prefixes, 4) temporarily route heavy traffic to a smaller model to reduce memory. Thoughts?

leo (network): capacity check: eu-west1-a has spare GPU capacity in the dedicated pool but autoscaler is slow. We can scale pool + warm nodes but that will take ~6-8m. Cross-region failover to eu-central is sub-100ms extra latency for most requests.

sofia (eng-runtime): runtime can issue a KV prefix purge for the top offenders — we can evict per-session prefixes. I can run a safe purge that targets sessions older than X and session size > Y. That should reduce memory footprint quickly.

raj (sre): before purging, let's snapshot top keys to S3 for postmortem. Running `kvscan --region=eu-west1 --top=500 > /tmp/top_keys.json`

emma (oncall): do the snapshot. we'll attempt purge + scale. fallback to region failover if still unhealthy. Also enable temporary routing to model-compat m-small for requests exceeding token-length 8k — that should reduce per-session KV retention.

sofia (eng-runtime): snapshot complete. starting purge command:
```
# purge large stale prefixes (safe mode)
kvctl purge --region eu-west1 --age 10m --min-size 1MB --dry-run=false --snapshot /tmp/top_keys.json
```

sam (prod): heads-up: a handful of enterprise customers in EU are on sessions with long sequences. if we redirect them to a smaller model we might see quality regressions. coordinate with CS.

ana (customer-success): drafting message: "We've detected elevated errors impacting inference for some EU customers. We're executing mitigations that may temporarily affect response quality for long-running sessions. We'll follow up within 30 minutes."

emma (oncall): good. starting scaling now: leo please issue pool scale. raj/sofia watch worker restarts.

leo (network): issuing scale: `infractl dedicated scale --pool eu-west1-a --gpus +4 --priority emergency` — started. ETA ~7m to ready.

opsbot: Deploy queue message: dedicated pool scale requested by leo. Request ID req-9087.

sofia (eng-runtime): purge ran. initial metrics show KV cache size dropping ~22% over 2m. mlworker OOMs dropped to near zero but some workers still restarting due to corrupted sessions.

raj (sre): restarting problematic mlworker pods one by one to avoid thundering herd: `kubectl delete pod mlworker-2 -n inference --grace-period=30` then monitor.

emma (oncall): monitoring latencies and 5xx. any improvement on gateway?

sofia (eng-runtime): gateway 5xx rate down to 2.1% from 7.4% — trending down. error types now primarily 504 timeouts vs OOMs.

leo (network): dedicated capacity is coming online (2/4 nodes ready) — median readiness time 4m more.

sam (prod): should we start a controlled traffic shift back to eu-west1 once nodes warmed? or leave shifted?

emma (oncall): let's keep current routing. no full cross-region failover yet. we'll do a tight canary reintroduce when pool is fully ready.

ana (customer-success): posted preliminary customer note to affected customers. included impact window and mitigation status.

sofia (eng-runtime): running a targeted graceful drain handshake to avoid in-flight session loss — sending drain signal to edgepool instances and setting `X-Prefer-Fallback: eu-central` header for new requests above token threshold. snippet:
```
# graceful drain command
gatewayctl drain --pool eu-west1-a --mode graceful --timeout 180s --drain-hint X-Prefer-Fallback=eu-central
```

raj (sre): verifying that the drain handshake honored sticky sessions. running `gatewayctl show-handshake eu-west1-a` shows 92% handshake success, 8% refused (these are long pinned sessions).

emma (oncall): for the 8% refused, route them to compatible fallback in-region: `eu-central-compat` to avoid cross-continental latency. Leo, can you add a temporary steering rule?

leo (network): adding rule: `route-rule add --from eu-west1-a --to eu-central-compat --match 'session.pinned==true && seq_len>8000' --priority 1000` — applied.

sofia (eng-runtime): new rule in effect. log shows `handshake-refused` sessions now being diverted. KV cache pressure stabilizing.

opsbot: Incident note: mitigation actions applied: KV purge, pool scale +4 GPUs, graceful drain handshake, temporary routing rule to eu-central-compat.

emma (oncall): current status: 5xx rate 0.6% (near baseline), mlworker restart rate nominal, dedicated nodes still warming. recommendation: keep temporary routing + scale until tomorrow + follow-up postmortem. any objections?

sam (prod): prepare a rollback plan if quality complaints rise. we'll add intercept in support playbook to revert routing per-customer.

ana (customer-success): will monitor customer inbox; prioritizing flagged enterprise customers.

raj (sre): collecting artifacts: `kubectl logs` dumps, kv snapshots, pod restart times, gateway trace ids. uploading to /postmortem/4441000000/

sofia (eng-runtime): adding music note: runtime team will add an automated eviction policy to prevent long-tail sessions from causing OOM in the future (RFC in next sprint).

emma (oncall): thanks team. I'll mark incident status as mitigated (watching) and do formal handoff to oncall-next. shifting to follow-up mode.

incident-bot: Incident 4441000000 status changed to MITIGATED by emma (oncall). severity: sev2. page to oncall-next scheduled.

emma (oncall): handing off to raj for postmortem + timeline. leaving a short checklist in the incident doc.

raj (sre): acknowledged. will own postmortem and timeline; will include root cause hypothesis around long-lived sessions + insufficient eviction policy + slow autoscaler.

sofia (eng-runtime): adding a follow-up item: add per-session size cap and better telemetry for prefix growth.

leo (network): follow-up: improve scale-up warm path for dedicated pools to <3m.
